the identification of factors at multiple levels of influence that may be amenable to intervention and/or policy change to increase active transportation among children and youth.
the identification of correlates of active travel to school and the implications of this for policy and planning.
the role that individual-, school-, and neighborhood-level factors play in determining the extent to which youth engage in active transportation to and from school.

active transportation to school is related to individual, family, neighborhood, school, and policy factors, and that a multi-level approach is needed to fully understand the determinants of active transportation.
